artworks.title: La Nuit (Night)
artworks.description: An oil painting by the French academic master William-Adolphe Bouguereau personifying Night as a graceful female figure gliding through the darkened sky, her dark veil billowing about her. It belongs to a group of allegorical canvases Bouguereau devoted to the times of day, rendering the ancient goddess of night in the polished idiom of nineteenth-century academic painting.

artworks.title: Night and Sleep
artworks.description: An oil painting by the English artist Evelyn De Morgan, now in the De Morgan Foundation collection. Nyx, the goddess of night, drifts across the sky drawing her mantle of darkness over the world, while her son Hypnos floats at her side scattering the poppies of sleep. The intertwined pair show De Morgan's debt to Botticelli and the Pre-Raphaelites.

artworks.title: Nyx, Night Goddess
artworks.description: Moreau's Symbolist Nyx rises as a jewelled vision of primordial Night — dark wings, star-dust, and the hush before dreaming. The painting names the Hesiodic goddess directly rather than a generic allegory of evening.

artworks.title: Night
artworks.description: Burne-Jones personifies Night as a solemn, draped woman drifting through a star-pricked void — Pre-Raphaelite stillness for the goddess who mothers Sleep and Death. Watercolour and bodycolour; a Victorian heir to the ancient Nyx.

artworks.title: Night
artworks.description: Michelangelo's marble Night reclines on the tomb of Giuliano de' Medici in Florence's New Sacristy — owl, mask, and poppies at her side. Renaissance allegory of Night that later ages read through the face of Nyx herself.

music.title: Nyx
music.description: Salonen's symphonic poem names the primordial goddess directly — Night as orchestral darkness, commissioned for Paris, London, Atlanta, and Carnegie Hall.

popCulture.title: Hades
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: Supergiant's Nyx is the House's foster mother — Night herself raising Zagreus in the dark, cooler and kinder than the Olympians above.

popCulture.title: Hades II
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: She remains a pillar of the underworld household in the sequel — Night watching Melinoë's war with the same quiet authority.

popCulture.title: Persona 3
popCulture.creator: Atlus
popCulture.description: Atlus makes Nyx the final cosmic threat — the primordial Night as the apocalypse the protagonists must face at the end of the school year.

popCulture.title: Nox (mythology)
popCulture.description: Rome's Nox is Nyx under a Latin name — Night as a goddess still listed among the powers even Zeus feared to anger.
